problem: UMI-style handheld data collection with only wrist cameras under-observes global context for mobile manipulation, while naively adding egocentric head cameras and 6-DoF head actions creates large visual and kinematic human-to-robot embodiment gaps. Prior egocentric systems therefore need robot teleoperation data or are limited to fixed-base setups or robots with custom 6-DoF necks.
motivation: Robot teleoperation for mobile manipulators is expensive and hard to scale, while robot-free human demonstrations are portable and scalable. Whole-body mobile manipulation needs global context, navigation and active perception, which require an egocentric view, so the embodiment gap it introduces must be bridged explicitly.
key_idea: Add a head-mounted camera to bimanual UMI and bridge the embodiment gap with an embodiment-agnostic 3D egocentric representation in a gripper-centric frame, a relaxed 3D look-at-point head action, and a constraint-aware whole-body IK controller, so policies trained only on human demos run on a mobile robot.
insight: The ablations show that both wrist and head views are needed (Head-Only gets 0% on laundry, 5% on delivery). Naive RGB plus 6-DoF head action fails (RGB-Only gets 0% on two tasks, 45% on delivery) because of OOD viewpoint and appearance shifts and kinematically infeasible head commands. Removing the active neck cuts success (75%, 55%, 55%), and the look-at abstraction also lets operators of different heights (167 cm and 182 cm) transfer.
method: HoMMI data collection: three iPhones (two on UMI-style grippers, one on a cap) share an ARKit coordinate frame and record RGB, depth, 6-DoF pose and gripper width at 60 Hz. Tracking error is under 5 mm and 0.8°.

3D visual representation: head pointmap patchified to 16x16 patches, DINOv3 patch features concatenated with a sinusoidal encoding of the 3D point, arm points masked (z<0 in gripper frames), attention pooling to an ego embedding. Wrist images use CLS tokens from a shared finetuned dinov3-vitb16.
Look-at point action: head action is a 3D point (ray-pointmap intersection in training). At inference a head controller builds a feasible neck rotation pointing at it, separate from the IK.
Gripper-centric frame: gripper poses, pointmaps and look-at points are all expressed in the left-gripper frame, so the policy is invariant to head motion and height.
Diffusion Policy with a DiT backbone: To=2, Tp=32 at 20 Hz, 23-D action (2x9 gripper pose, 3 look-at, 2 widths), DDIM sampling.

Constraint-aware whole-body IK (Mink QP, 100 Hz): high-weight bimanual SE(3) tracking, nominal and current posture regularization, CoM-over-base task, and constraints on joint and base velocity, self-collision and torso upright. Commands are interpolated between the 10 Hz policy and the 500 Hz robot loop.
Asynchronous inference: a detached policy server plus a real-time bridge with latency-corrected observations, stale-action filtering and a scheduled action buffer.

setting.backbone: Diffusion Policy (DiT) with a finetuned DINOv3 ViT-B/16 encoder, trained from human demos
setting.training_data: Robot-free human UMI+ego demonstrations only: 200 (laundry), 166 (delivery), 115 (tablescape); no robot teleop data
setting.observation: Head RGB + pointmap (stereo depth on the robot, iPhone depth for human data), two wrist RGB, and proprioception
setting.action_space: Bimanual end-effector 6D poses, gripper widths and a 3D head look-at point; a whole-body IK controller outputs joint and holonomic base commands

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark. Real-robot success rates are given only in a figure (20 rollouts per task) and quoted in the text: Ours 90% laundry, 85% delivery, 80% tablescape.
results: HoMMI reaches 90% (laundry), 85% (delivery) and 80% (tablescape) success over 20 real-robot rollouts each. Wrist-Only (UMI) gets 15% on delivery, RGB-Only gets 45% on delivery and 0% on two tasks, and Head-Only gets 0% (laundry) and 5% (delivery). Ablating the active neck gives 75%, 55% and 55%.
limitations: Short observation history (To=2) limits recovery and handling of partial observability in long-horizon tasks
Vision-only, with no force or tactile sensing or compliance control
A residual hardware embodiment gap remains, and evaluation is limited to three tasks with 20 rollouts each
